def-bv-algebra-and-degree-plus-one-brack:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$. A unital $\mathbb Z$-graded associative $k$-algebra
$A=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}A^r$ is **graded commutative** when its unit $1$ has
degree $0$ and homogeneous $a,b$ satisfy $ab=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$. A linear map
$\Delta:A^r\to A^{r+1}$ is a **BV generator of degree $+1$** when
$\Delta(1)=0$, $\Delta^2=0$, and it has order at most two in the following
graded-commutator convention. For homogeneous operators $P,Q$, set
$$[P,Q]=PQ-(-1)^{|P||Q|}QP,$$
and for homogeneous $a\in A$ let $m_a(x)=ax$. The order condition is
$$\left[\left[\left[\Delta,m_a\right],m_b\right],m_c\right]=0$$
for all homogeneous $a,b,c\in A$. The pair $(A,\Delta)$ with these data is a
**BV algebra in the degree-$+1$ convention**. Its derived bracket is the
bilinear operation of degree $+1$
$$\{a,b\}=(-1)^{|a|}\bigl(\Delta(ab)-(\Delta a)b-(-1)^{|a|}a\Delta b\bigr)$$
on homogeneous elements, extended by linearity.

This item fixes the grading, commutator order condition, and bracket formula.
It does not include a separate differential $Q$ or assert compatibility with
one. The associated odd-skew, biderivation, and Jacobi identities are proved in
[[thm-bv-derived-bracket-is-odd-poisson]].
def-classical-lie-action-brst-complex:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, let $\mathfrak g$ be a Lie algebra over
$k$, and let $A$ be a unital commutative $k$-algebra. A **classical
Lie-action BRST input** is a Lie algebra homomorphism
$\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_k(A)$ whose values are derivations:
for $x\in\mathfrak g$ and $a,b\in A$,
$$\rho(x)(ab)=\rho(x)(a)b+a\rho(x)(b),\qquad \rho(x)(1)=0.$$
In particular, $A$ is a $\mathfrak g$-module, so its Chevalley–Eilenberg
cochains are
$$C^n_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathfrak g,A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\Lambda^n\mathfrak g,A)\quad(n\geq0),$$
and are zero for $n<0$. Define the degree-$+1$ **classical Lie-action BRST
operator** by the fixed zero-based formula
$$\begin{aligned}(d_{\mathrm{BRST}}f)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)={}&\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i\rho(x_i)f(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_n)\\&+\sum_{0\leq i<j\leq n}(-1)^{i+j}f([x_i,x_j],x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_n).\end{aligned}$$
A hat denotes omission; the bracket is inserted first. This is exactly the
Chevalley–Eilenberg differential for the stated representation, with the
BRST name reserved here for this classical Lie-action model.

Its square-zero property and the resulting quotient cohomology are established
in [[thm-classical-lie-action-brst-differential-squares-zero]]. This model does
not claim a Koszul–Tate resolution, a BFV charge for arbitrary first-class
constraints, reducible or open gauge algebras, field-dependent structure
functions, or quantum BRST cohomology.
thm-bv-derived-bracket-is-odd-poisson:
## Statement

Let $(A,\Delta)$ be as in [[def-bv-algebra-and-degree-plus-one-bracket]].
For homogeneous $a,b,c\in A$, the derived bracket has degree
$|\{a,b\}|=|a|+|b|+1$ and satisfies
$$\{a,b\}=-(-1)^{(|a|+1)(|b|+1)}\{b,a\},$$
$$\{a,bc\}=\{a,b\}c+(-1)^{(|a|+1)|b|}b\{a,c\},$$
and
$$\{a,\{b,c\}\}=\{\{a,b\},c\}+(-1)^{(|a|+1)(|b|+1)}\{b,\{a,c\}\}.$$
Thus it is an odd Poisson bracket, meaning an odd-skew bracket that is a
derivation in each argument and satisfies the displayed odd Jacobi identity.
def-classical-and-formal-quantum-master-:
## Definition

Let $(A,\Delta)$ be a BV algebra in the degree-$+1$ convention of
[[def-bv-algebra-and-degree-plus-one-bracket]], with derived bracket $\{-,-\}$.
For an element $S\in A^0$, the **classical master equation** (CME) is
$$\{S,S\}=0.$$

For a formal version, take $A$ over $\mathbb C$, let $\hbar$ be a central
formal variable of degree $0$, and write $A[\![\hbar]\!]$ for formal power series
with the Cauchy product. Extend $\Delta$ and $\{-,-\}$ coefficientwise. For
$S_\hbar\in A^0[\![\hbar]\!]$, the **formal quantum master equation** (QME) in
the convention used here is
$$\frac12\{S_\hbar,S_\hbar\}-i\hbar\Delta S_\hbar=0$$
as an equality in $A^1[\![\hbar]\!]$, checked coefficientwise. Each coefficient
uses only a finite Cauchy sum, so this is a formal algebraic condition and
requires no analytic convergence.
thm-classical-lie-action-brst-differenti:
## Statement

For every classical Lie-action BRST input of
[[def-classical-lie-action-brst-complex]] and every $n\geq0$,
$$d_{\mathrm{BRST}}^{n+1}d_{\mathrm{BRST}}^n=0.$$
Consequently, the quotient
$$H^n_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathfrak g,A):=\ker(d_{\mathrm{BRST}}^n)/\operatorname{im}(d_{\mathrm{BRST}}^{n-1})$$
is a well-defined vector space, with $C^{-1}_{\mathrm{BRST}}=0$.
thm-classical-master-equation-defines-sq:
## Statement

Let $(A,\Delta)$ be as in [[def-bv-algebra-and-degree-plus-one-bracket]], and
let $S\in A^0$ satisfy the classical master equation in
[[def-classical-and-formal-quantum-master-equations]]. Then
$d_S:A\to A$, $d_S(a)=\{S,a\}$, has degree $+1$ and satisfies $d_S^2=0$.
